newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spot end up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spot end up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Monday with investors borrowing money on the market to prepare for trading in new domestic A shares debuting this week, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose to 10.30 percent from 8.51 percent last Friday.
Combined turnover rose to 7.98 million lots from 4.35 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Hainan Overseas Chinese Investment Co will list domestic A shares on Tuesday and Anhui Heli Co on Wednesday. Liaoning Jingdi Construction Group Co will issue A shares on Wednesday.
"The rates for early-maturing contracts are expected to continue to be firm in the next couple of days due to funds needed for trading in new shares," one trader said.

Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up due to institutional bargain-hunting after prices had fallen for weeks, traders said. The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 rose to 121.75 yuan from 121.29 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market rose to 3.15 million lots from 2.03 million.
Traders expect spot prices to consolidate in a narrow range in the next few days. -- Shanghai newsroom (86-21) 6279-7004
